summary: PANDA Radboud-style fine Gleason annotation contract with provider-specific provenance and protected unknown/background.

annotation_traits: Radboud masks encode background/unknown, stroma, benign epithelium, and Gleason patterns 3, 4, and 5
Karolinska masks use a different coarse annotation convention
the public challenge includes incomplete, sparse, and noisy annotations
semantic_limitations: This profile is only valid for a verified Radboud-style fine mask; Karolinska binary cancer annotations are not interchangeable.
Background/unknown cannot be interpreted as benign stroma or available tissue.
Necrosis, immune, vessel, and other-tissue compartments are not separately encoded.

rules.claim: Use this profile only for verified Radboud-style fine masks; do not apply its six-class meaning to Karolinska-style coarse masks.
rules.required_observation: Verify provider, preprocessing revision, label-map digest, and observed fine-ID signature before planning.
counterexamples: Reading Karolinska label 2 as stroma or benign epithelium under the Radboud contract.
Inferring provider from prostate organ metadata.
known_limitations: The current provenance checker verifies presence; a certified profile router must additionally validate allowed provider values.

rules.claim: Preserve label 0 exactly because it includes background, unknown, and potentially unannotated regions rather than a source tissue class.
rules.required_observation: Verify no source/target component or changed pixel belongs to the zero footprint.
counterexamples: Expanding a Gleason region into unlabeled tissue.
Backfilling a sparse unknown gap with stroma before tumor expansion.
expected_morphology: The source zero footprint remains pixel-identical.
forbidden_morphology: Unknown-label filling, seeding, crossing, or cleanup.
known_limitations: An unlabeled H&E region may contain tissue; this profile still cannot authorize editing it.

rules.claim: A Gleason label represents tumor architecture, not merely tumor presence or mask color; local H&E must support the retained pattern.
rules.required_observation: Inspect whether glands are discrete and well formed, fused/poorly formed/cribriform/glomeruloid, or solid/single-cell/comedonecrotic before ranking an interface.
exceptions: A burden-only boundary displacement may retain the existing fine label only where adjacent H&E resembles the same component.
counterexamples: Extending Gleason 3 over a solid H&E focus.
Extending Gleason 5 into a field of separate well-formed glands.
expected_morphology: Pattern 4: fused, poorly formed, cribriform, or glomeruloid architecture.
Pattern 5: solid sheets, cords, single cells, or comedonecrosis.
forbidden_morphology: A fine label expanded across visibly incompatible architecture.
known_limitations: Architectural assessment needs sufficient H&E resolution and expert validation.

rules.claim: Do not perform an implicit Gleason transition during a generic tumor burden edit.
rules.required_observation: Audit every changed source and target fine ID against the selected component's existing pattern and primitive contract.
exceptions: A dedicated pattern-transition primitive with a separate H&E morphology contract.
counterexamples: Changing pattern 3 to pattern 4 while increasing only tumor area.
Collapsing all patterns to canonical Tumor in the saved fine mask.
expected_morphology: Unrequested Gleason components retain fine IDs exactly.
forbidden_morphology: Silent grade upgrade, downgrade, or fine-to-coarse collapse.

rules.claim: Do not bridge, fill, or connect sparse annotated regions merely to make the tumor mask look complete.
rules.required_observation: Compare source/target component and hole topology and preserve all unrequested labels.
exceptions: An independently reviewed annotation-repair task outside mask edit.
counterexamples: Joining separate pattern-4 regions across unknown pixels.
Filling unlabeled holes inside a tumor component.
expected_morphology: The edit deforms one selected existing interface without repairing unrelated annotation gaps.
forbidden_morphology: New bridges, islands, merges, splits, or hole filling.
known_limitations: Quantitative sparsity envelopes must be learned separately by provider and split.
